You'll own the relationships on each side, turn what you hear into pilots and launches, and keep every team involved pointed at the same goals.
 You'll decide what to test, how to measure it and whether a pilot should scale, change direction or stop.
 AI should be part of how you work. Use it to research, draft, analyse and automate. You're responsible for the quality of the result.
 What we value
 Sound judgement and attention to detail.
 Owning results, not activity, and finishing work without being chased.
 Running a small test this week over perfecting a plan for a month.
 Letting evidence change your mind.
 The honesty to stop a pilot that isn't working, including your own.
 What you'll do
 Take new initiatives from idea to launch 
 For each initiative, define the problem, the hypothesis, the smallest useful test and what success looks like. Set the success metrics before anything starts.
 Run pilots end to end with partners and customers. Use product, call and commercial data to judge the result, then recommend whether to scale, change direction or stop, and back that recommendation with evidence.
 Own the partner and customer relationships

 Keep the teams aligned

 Make what works repeatable 
 When an initiative succeeds, build the processes, playbooks and documentation that let Sadie run it at scale without you in every conversation.

 Product sense. You can form a view on where a product should go and explain why it matters to customers and the business.

 Work in a technology company

 Hospitality, hotel technology or travel
 Partnerships with technology or integration partners

We believe independent restaurants deserve the same advantages as big chains without giving up their independence.
 Ilir Sela started Slice in his family’s pizzerias, where he saw firsthand what it takes to run a local shop. Now we’re taking everything we’ve learned beyond pizza, to taquerias, delis, burger joints, and other neighborhood staples.
 We put technology, marketing, buying power, and support to work for more than 15,000 restaurants, so owners spend less time on admin, marketing, and order management and more time growing their business. They remain independent, but never alone.
 We’re growing our team to help bring this next chapter to life. That’s where you come in.
 The Challenge to Solve 
 Slice’s Services teams build the backend systems, APIs, integrations, and operational capabilities that power our platform. We are looking for a high-agency Engineering Manager who can identify the most valuable problems, turn ambiguity into clear direction, and build a team capable of delivering exceptional results. This is not a coordination-only role. You will stay close to the technology, product, and customer. You will be accountable for both your team's performance and the impact it creates. Management is a force multiplier—not another layer of process.
 Your role is to create the conditions in which talented engineers can do the best work of their careers. That means setting a clear mission, raising standards, removing obstacles, developing judgment, and holding yourself and others accountable.
 Putting people first does not mean avoiding difficult conversations or lowering the bar. It means giving people meaningful ownership, direct feedback, strong support, and the opportunity to grow.
 Our strongest managers:
 Focus teams on customer outcomes rather than activity.
 Create clarity when the path is uncertain.
 Make decisions with incomplete information and adapt quickly.
 Stay close to the details without becoming the bottleneck.
 Challenge assumptions and look for asymmetric opportunities.
 Build trust through candor, consistency, and follow-through.
 Take responsibility for outcomes, including when things go wrong.
 The Role 
 Own customer and business outcomes 
 Partner with Product, Design, Data, and Operations to identify the problems most worth solving. Define success through measurable value for pizzerias, customers, and the business—not projects completed or code shipped.
 Lead technical direction 
 Guide architecture and engineering decisions across the services your team owns. Help the team balance speed, reliability, simplicity, and long-term system health.
 Our services are converging on Python, while parts of our ecosystem use Go and Ruby. We choose technology based on the problem and the customer value it enables—not preference or fashion.
 You should be comfortable leading teams working with:
 Python, Go, and Ruby services.
 APIs, distributed systems, and asynchronous workflows.
 Databases, AWS, observability, and production operations.
 Service migrations, reliability, security, and performance.
 Build a high-agency team 
 Give engineers context, clear decision boundaries, and meaningful ownership. Expect them to move with urgency, exercise judgment, raise issues early, and own what happens in production.
 When the team is blocked, work across boundaries and find a path forward rather than simply escalating the problem.
 Raise execution standards 
 Help the team deliver valuable improvements frequently without sacrificing quality. Reduce unnecessary ceremony, make risk visible, and build lightweight mechanisms that improve focus and learning.
 Use customer feedback, product data, incidents, and operational metrics to understand whether the team’s decisions are working.
 Develop exceptional people 
 Hire and retain outstanding engineers, including those from unconventional backgrounds who demonstrate unusual ability and drive.
 Coach engineers across experience levels, recognize future leaders, reward strong performance, and address underperformance clearly and promptly.
 Lead across Slice 
 Build strong relationships with other engineering, product, and business leaders. Influence through judgment and results rather than hierarchy.
 Surface disagreement directly, resolve it constructively, and optimize for Slice and its customers—not only your own team.
 The Team 
 You will lead engineers working on services that power key Slice experiences. The team collaborates across the US, Canada, UK, and North Macedonia, alongside partners in Product, Design, Data, and Operations.
 We value thoughtful asynchronous communication, direct discussion, and high-quality written decisions. Geography should not determine who has context, influence, or ownership.
 You will report to an Engineering Director and work with other managers and technical leaders to raise the standard across Slice Engineering.
 The Winning Recipe 
 We care more about evidence of impact, judgment, and trajectory than a perfectly conventional background.
 Strong candidates will bring:
 Experience building and operating customer-facing software or platforms.
 Experience managing high-performing engineering teams.
 Strong technical judgment across backend services, APIs, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, and production operations.
 Experience with Python, Go, Ruby, or comparable backend technologies.
 A record of improving both customer outcomes and engineering effectiveness.
 The ability to turn complex, ambiguous problems into clear direction.
 A founder-minded approach: resourceful, decisive, intellectually curious, and unwilling to wait for perfect conditions.
 Strong instincts for leverage—knowing when to move quickly and when deeper investment is necessary.
 The courage to challenge weak thinking, including your own.
 Clear, direct communication across technical and non-technical audiences.
 Low ego, high standards, and a strong sense of personal accountability.
 You will be succeeding when:
 Your team understands the customer outcomes it owns.
 Engineers operate with increasing independence, judgment, and urgency.
 Valuable improvements reach customers frequently.
 Systems become simpler, more reliable, and easier to evolve.
 High performers are growing and choosing to stay.
 Performance problems are addressed rather than allowed to compound.
 Cross-functional partners trust the team to solve difficult problems.
 Slice creates more value for pizzerias because your team exists.
 The Extras 
 Benefits include:
 Medical, dental, and vision plans.
 Flexible working hours.
 Generous time-off policies.
 Employee well-being allowance for eligible employees.
 Market-leading maternity and paternity schemes.
 Compensation package: $150k-$175k CAD base, plus benefits. Benefits may vary by location.
 The Hiring Process 
 Application.
 30-minute introductory conversation.
 60-minute conversation with an Engineering Director.
 Two leadership and technical interviews with future peers and team members.
 Conversation with our Head of RnD.
 Offer.

Purpose of the Job
The Vice President, Integration Management Office (IMO) is accountable for the end-to-end execution of the Bank's enterprise integration, bringing two established Canadian banking businesses together into a stronger, more efficient and more competitive combined bank. The IMO holds one integrated master plan, central value case objectives & realization, and a central view of program budget, setting the standards, decision gates, data and reporting that delivery teams work to. The IMO operates through a matrix of employees and consultants across the Bank, with the central programme office team and dedicated consultants reporting directly to the Vice President.
This is a cross-bank role. The Integration Management Office is the connective tissue between the Executive Leadership Team, the executive sponsors who own each workstream's outcomes, the Board and its committees, the Bank's regulators, and the vendor providing transition services. The Vice President sets the cadence, the control structure and the reporting spine those audiences rely on, and converts complexity into decisions and execution plans.
The role is deliberately broad rather than deep. Executive sponsors drive the substance within their own domains; the Vice President is accountable for the integrity of the whole across critical path, value case, risk management, and outcome accountability, including the judgment of when to verify, escalate, problem solve, or hold the line rather than absorb the work centrally.

Key Responsibilities - What You Will Lead: Own the integrated master plan and the critical path across every workstream, delivery organisation and partner, holding the baseline, the change control discipline and the monthly re-forecast.
 Hold the value case objectives as a controlled instrument that enforces outcome accountability to named owners with accounting discipline via supporting Finance partnership.
 Own a single integration budget view across every workstream and initiative, making cost-to-complete a live number and carrying integration budget and value capture into the Financial planning cycles.
 Chair the funding pathway. Run the investment gate that tests both the business case and the readiness to execute before a recommendation reaches the Integration Steering Committee, and recommend funding approval only against approved scope, cost, value and design.
 Direct the design authority that bounds scope before design begins, keeping the technology agenda proportionate and separating what must be delivered now from what can defer or sits outside integration scope and budget entirely.
 Run execution governance on a disciplined cadence and decision rights: a single register of risks, issues, dependencies and decisions spanning Bank-wide workstreams, with defined escalation thresholds into the Steering Committee, executive leadership and the Board.
 Govern the transition services exit calendar and the operating relationship with the external provider, treating exits as a commercial, cost and operating-model question - not only a technology sequencing exercise.
 Act as the single front door for integration-related regulatory engagement and content preparedness to ensure complete, consistent and finalized content via reviews, accountability tracking, and strong governance.
 Lead change management and people readiness for the combined bank, with change impact drawn from the same designs that drive the plan and employee readiness sequenced to customer conversion events rather than project milestones.
 Own the reporting spine so that the Steering Committee pack, the executive update and the quarterly Board report are drawn from the same underlying data, and lead the Integration Management Office team, its capacity model and its capability build.
Project Focus - Where You’ll Make Your Mark: Complete the stand-up of the next-generation Integration Management Office: delivery leads assigned across every integration and cross-functional workstream, a governance cadence that produces decisions, clearly understood and communicated plans, and programme reporting that clearly indicates where focus is required and when outcomes are realized.
 Establish and hold the integration baseline - a prioritised roadmap, ratified critical paths and an endorsed value plan the whole Bank can execute against.
 Land platform convergence: the migration and unification of EQ Bank & PCF customers and products onto a single set of systems, brand, channels, and experience that is delivered through a sequenced build, test and phased migration approach at significant scale.
 Carry integration budget and value capture through Financial planning cycles, in an environment where total & competing demands will exceed capacity and deliberate choices and trade-offs are part of the craft.
 Drive the value case, delivering the committed benefits of the transaction within the approved integration investment envelope.
 Deliver the transition services exit programme on or ahead of schedule, resolving the commercial and technical dependencies that sit between the Bank and each exit.
 Meet regulatory commitments on the dates given, and hold the risk and compliance side of the integration - enterprise risk, non-financial risk and compliance, financial crime, risk data and analytics, and treasury risk controls (and many others) - to the delivery and risk appetite standards.
 Champion the customer voice through every event: advocacy, contact centre service levels and platform availability alongside deposit, card and cross-sell growth, with adoption measured after each go-live and fed back into the value case.
Team and Collaboration - How You’ll Influence: Partner with the Executive Leadership Team and executive sponsors of workstreams as the leader who convenes, constructively challenges and closes, without assuming ownership of their scope.
 Consistently and accurately represent the integration progress and risks both internally and externally across Governance bodies, Board of Directors, integration and services partners, and regulators (as required).
 Hold every delivery partner and consulting firm to one integrated plan, one runbook set and one readiness standard, and govern statements of work against scope, rates and deliverable acceptance.
 Interlock with the business and technology delivery organisations so that capability, budget and resource stay aligned as work moves between them.
 Lead, shape and evolve, and coach the Integration Management Office team and a federated network of delivery leads across the Bank.
 Build the credibility, capability and energy of the Integration Management Office as the trusted centre of the integration, and make it a destination for people who want to do this work.
Let's Talk About You! : Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Engineering, Economics or a related field; MBA or advanced degree preferred.
 15+ years leading large-scale transformation, post-merger integration or enterprise program delivery within banking or financial services, including accountability for programs at a nine-figure investment scale.
 Demonstrated ownership of an integration through conversion - transition service exits, platform convergence and customer migration.
 Deep program management craft: integrated planning and critical path, gated funding, benefits realization, delivery assurance and portfolio prioritization in a regulated environment.
 Risk management fluency across all risk disciplines, with particular strength in execution risk, and the credibility to engage enterprise risk, non-financial risk, financial crime and compliance leaders on their own ground.
 Regulatory and Board-level engagement experience with prudential supervisors, Board committees, auditors and rating agencies.
 Customer-centric change leadership: a record of protecting customer experience, service levels and growth through conversion and migration events.
 Strong financial acumen - business cases, synergy taxonomy, cost-to-complete and forecast discipline exercised in partnership with Finance rather than parallel to it.
 Executive presence and the communication range to move between a workstream stand-up, a regulator meeting and a Board committee in the same day.
 Structured judgment about depth: able to test and assure work across a wide surface without displacing the leaders accountable for it.
Job Complexities & Thinking Challenges: The mandate spans the whole bank while the authority is largely indirect; outcomes are achieved through sponsors, delivery leads and partners who report elsewhere.
 Calibrating depth is the defining daily judgment - engaging far enough to know whether a plan is real, and stopping short of taking it over.
 Integration, the efficiency agenda and growth compete for the same senior leaders, so capacity rather than ambition is the binding constraint on what can be committed.
 External audiences have different needs and cannot be served by a single message: the regulator needs consistency and an evidence trail, commercial counterparties have their own priorities, and the Board needs numbers that are clear and consistent.
 Value is easy to assert and hard to prove; the same outcome can be claimed by several programmes unless attribution rules are enforced.
 The IMO operates through a matrix of employees and consultants across the Bank, with the central programme office team and dedicated consultants reporting directly to the Vice President.
 Navigate transformational change where consequential decisions must be made with incomplete information and immovable conversion dates and service terminations require disciplined agility and problem-solving to achieve.

Ces solutions vont au-delà des assistants conversationnels traditionnels en permettant à des agents intelligents d'analyser des données, de raisonner, de prendre des décisions, d'orchestrer des workflows complexes et d'interagir avec plusieurs systèmes d'entreprise de manière autonome et sécurisée.
 Nous recherchons une personne occupant un rôle d’Architecte Sécurité Données - IA Générative et Agentique pour rejoindre notre équipe à Québec, spécialisée dans la gestion des connaissances. Notre équipe multidisciplinaire se concentre sur la collecte, la transformation et l’enrichissement des données. Nos projets impliquent la définition et le déploiement de chaînes de traitement automatisées pour rendre les données accessibles aux utilisateurs. Avec le soutien de nos scientifiques de données, l'équipe conçoit, entraîne et intègre des modèles d’intelligence artificielle, y compris l'IA générative (GenAI) basée sur des grands modèles de langue (LLM), afin d’améliorer l’analyse des données.  La personne titulaire du poste Architecte Sécurité Données - IA Générative et Agentique jouera un rôle clé dans la conception, le développement et la mise en production de plateformes et applications intelligentes intégrant des modèles de langage (LLM), des architectures multi-agents, des moteurs RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation), des outils d'orchestration et des services cloud de nouvelle génération. WHO ARE WE?

WHY THIS ROLE?

We're building the foundational infrastructure that will define how the world thinks about and deploys AI, and we want the sharpest, most driven, and most curious people to help us do it. As the founding lead of Agentic Analytics, a new team in our Analytics and Data Insights organization, you'll own how Cohere gets answers from its own data: an agentic analytics system that answers business questions over governed data, shows the source, query, and freshness behind every answer, and asks for clarification or declines when the evidence is insufficient.

Agentic analytics is far from a solved problem, and correctness is the hard part. A query that runs can still answer the wrong question. Agents go wrong when a business term maps to more than one table, when data goes stale, and when the right context never reaches the model. The worst failures are silent and plausible: a join that double-counts, a wrong denominator, missing data read as zero. Getting this right takes governed definitions, context an agent can use, and an evaluation bar that decides what ships.

You'll build on work already in motion: an internal analytics agent in pilot on our BigQuery warehouse, which is fed by tested ingestion pipelines and modeled in dbt. In your first year, you'll take it to production for teams across Cohere, one domain at a time, and make it replicable: each new domain stands up with configuration, a fresh evaluation set, and very little new code.

This is a hands-on  staff engineering role reporting to our Senior Director of Data Analytics. You'll write production code and evaluation sets yourself while managing a small founding team that grows as the system proves itself. You may have held the title software engineer, AI engineer, or data scientist; what matters is that you've built a system like this and run it in production.

RESPONSIBILITIES

As the lead of Agentic Analytics, you will:

 - Own the system end to end. Set the architecture for how a business question becomes a governed query and a verifiable answer: interpreting the question, retrieving the right context, applying approved definitions and joins, enforcing the asking user's permissions, and attaching the evidence (source, query, freshness) to every answer.

 - Build and run it in production. Design the core services and write much of the first version yourself: agent-facing data tools (MCP or equivalent), context retrieval, agent skills for analytics, and the APIs that serve answers. Hold them to production standards for reliability, latency, cost, security, and observability. Put it where people already work: Slack, North, IDEs, and other agents.

 - Hold every release to the evaluation bar. Build and run the evaluation harness, and define what correct means in each domain: ground-truth question sets, including held-out cases and questions the agent should clarify or decline; result-level scoring, correct-or-decline rates, coverage, and error severity; and regression tests on every change to context, skills, or models. Nothing ships below the bar, and the call on when a domain is ready for production is yours.

 - Engineer the context layer. Turn metric definitions, approved joins, documentation generated from the code that builds each table, a business glossary, and worked examples into context the agent can use. Every correction becomes a reviewed definition and a regression test.

 - Roll it out across Cohere. Bring domains such as marketing, revenue, finance, and product onto the system one at a time, each with named owners, certified definitions, and its own evaluation set. Measure adoption, accuracy, turnaround, and correction effort against how those teams work today.

 - Make it replicable. Package the tools, skills, context templates, and evaluations, and document them well enough that other teams at Cohere can run the system without you.

 - Hire and lead the team. Bring on the team's first engineers, set the technical bar, review the work, and develop the people doing it.

 - Partner across Cohere. Work with our data platform team on the warehouse and semantic models, our model evaluation team on evaluation methodology, our security team on access, and each domain's owners on definitions and rollout.

QUALIFICATIONS

You may be a good fit, if you have:

 - 10+ years building and operating production analytics or software systems, including technical leadership of a team or of systems that span teams

 - Experience shipping LLM agents to production: tool use, MCP or similar, retrieval and context engineering, guardrails, and observability, with firm opinions on where they fail

 - Hands-on experience building natural-language or agentic analytics (text-to-SQL, analytics agents, question answering over a semantic layer) that real users relied on, and evidence that it was right

 - Depth in evaluating LLM systems: golden sets, result-level comparison, abstention metrics, error taxonomies, and regression testing in CI, plus the judgment to tell a good demo from a system you'd put in front of a CFO

 - Strong Python and SQL, and experience designing and running production services and APIs on a major cloud (Google Cloud is a plus)

 - Fluency with data: cloud warehouses (BigQuery, Snowflake, or similar), dbt, and semantic layers (MetricFlow, LookML, Cube, or similar). You think in grain, metric definitions, and approved joins, and you can tell when a number is wrong before it reaches a decision

 - Experience building identity-aware access for agents, where the agent acts with the asking user's permissions and every query leaves an audit trail

 - Experience hiring and developing engineers, with a leadership style grounded in empathy as much as in data

 - Genuine excitement about AI: you follow the research, have opinions, and enjoy being in the weeds

 - Comfort operating in ambiguity, leading through partners you don't manage, and writing design docs and eval reports that settle decisions across teams

If some of the above doesn't line up perfectly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply!

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

 - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

 - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

 - Annual enrichment benefits:
   
   

HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

 - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.

 - Monitor bank clearing accounts and coordinate with AP and other accounting team members to resolve exceptions and ensure accurate recording.

Month-End Closing & Financial Reporting

 - Support monthly, quarterly, and annual closing activities to ensure accurate and timely financial reporting

 - Perform AP aging reviews, account balance analysis, and variance investigations.

 - Review invoices received after the AP close, identify unrecorded expenses related to the prior accounting period, and prepare a monthly accrual report for the Senior Accountant’s review and journal entry posting.

 - Identify unusual transactions, discrepancies, and accounting issues, and recommend corrective actions.

 - Collaborate with the accounting team to ensure all assigned close deliverables are completed within established deadlines.

 Affirm runs its workloads on more than 85 Amazon EKS clusters, and the number is growing. The Workload Safety team creates one set of standards for how workloads are configured and run, so Affirm can grow globally and still meet its availability and latency SLOs. The team identifies the industry best practices Affirm needs, drives their adoption across every engineering team on EKS, and enforces them through policy and automation so new workloads comply by default. 
 As a senior engineer on the team, you will help set its roadmap, decide which standards matter most, and build a repeatable way to take each standard from research to enforcement across the fleet. 
 What you’ll do 
 Define and evolve workload safety standards for Affirm's EKS fleet, such as CPU and memory settings, workload isolation and placement, tolerance for disruption, graceful termination to name a few

 Fix stuck workloads and node lifecycle problems, such as pods that ignore termination signals, pod disruption budgets that block node cycling, and Karpenter timeouts that prevent bin packing and the removal of excess capacity

 Keep up with new best practices from the Kubernetes community and adapt them to Affirm's needs 
 What we look for

 Solid grasp of the pod lifecycle and disruption management, including graceful termination, pod disruption budgets, and node draining

BUILD SOMETHING PEOPLE LOVE

Wealthsimple is Canada’s leading financial innovator. The company offers a full suite of simple, sophisticated financial products across managed investing, do-it-yourself trading, cryptocurrency, tax filing, spending and saving. Wealthsimple currently serves more than 4 million Canadians and holds over $169 billion in assets under administration. The company was founded in 2014 by a team of financial experts and technology entrepreneurs, and is headquartered in Toronto, Canada.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Staff Product Manager to own Wealthsimple’s Connectivity Platform, spanning two critical areas:

 - Brokerage & Bank Linking: How clients securely and reliably connect external financial institutions to Wealthsimple.

 - Public API: How clients and partners securely access and use Wealthsimple financial data outside of Wealthsimple.

Together, these capabilities define how Wealthsimple connects to the broader financial ecosystem, and how every product team inside Wealthsimple builds on the external financial data that flows through it. This role will set the strategy for that platform and turn it into a reliable, scalable and differentiated capability for our clients, our product teams and our partners.

This is a platform role with a meaningful client experience surface. You’ll need to be equally comfortable thinking about APIs, data models and platform architecture as you are designing a client UX or deciding how Wealthsimple should work with an external provider.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Brokerage & Bank Linking team builds the technology that lets clients link their outside bank and brokerage accounts to Wealthsimple. It owns the automated and manual linking experiences end to end, along with the three connectors behind them: Plaid, Flinks, and WST, our own in-house connector. That makes it one of the highest leverage surfaces in the company, and powers a growing set of experiences built by other product teams.

WHAT YOU’LL OWN

Connectivity Strategy

 - Set the long term vision and strategy for how Wealthsimple connects with the broader financial ecosystem.

 - Define the capabilities we should build ourselves, where we should rely on partners, and where we can create differentiated client value.

 - Develop a roadmap that balances immediate product needs with investments in reusable platform capabilities.

Brokerage & Bank Linking

 - Own the end to end experience for connecting external bank and brokerage accounts to Wealthsimple — automated and manual, including how clients recover when an automated connection fails.

 - Improve connection success, reliability and coverage across institutions, and own the routing strategy that decides which connector handles which institution and flow.

 - Own the client experience, including institution selection, authentication, errors, recovery and connection management.

 - Drive reliability and AI Powered  self-healing so connections detect and recover from failure without manual intervention.

 - Balance conversion against fraud exposure and operational load, making those tradeoffs deliberately with our risk and operations partners.

 - Develop the platform capabilities that allow Wealthsimple products to consume external financial data consistently.

 - Own relationships and product integrations with connectivity vendors such as Plaid and Flinks, and decide where our own connector should lead — including how much of the connector business Wealthsimple should be in long term and where it makes more sense to partner.

Public API

 - Own the strategy and roadmap for Wealthsimple’s Public API and external data connectivity.

 - Make it safe and easy for clients to permission their Wealthsimple financial data to the products and services they choose.

 - Define the platform capabilities required for authentication, consent, permissions, data access and partner integrations.

 - Identify and prioritize the partners and use cases that matter most to Wealthsimple clients.

 - Build toward a world where Wealthsimple is the financial institution where clients have the most control over their financial data.

 - Accelerate wealthsimple and our industry toward open banking.

SKILLS YOU BRING

You’re a strong product thinker who can operate across platform infrastructure, external ecosystems and client experience. You likely have:

 - Experience owning a platform, API, developer product or integrations platform, with a track record on metric-attached outcomes like conversion, success rate or reliability — not only feature delivery.

 - Enough technical depth to work closely with engineers on APIs, authentication, data models, routing and platform architecture.

 - Experience delivering through external vendors or partners whose roadmaps you don’t control, including making thoughtful build versus buy decisions and holding vendors accountable for product outcomes.

 - Comfort treating reliability as product work — error taxonomies, failure recovery, observability, and the operational load a product creates.

 - Experience weighing growth against fraud, risk and compliance, and holding both sides of that tradeoff.

 - The ability to turn a collection of technical capabilities into a clear product strategy and compelling long term vision, and to make the case for investing in it.

 - Strong analytical instincts and comfort using data to understand reliability, conversion, coverage and product performance, including building the measurement where it doesn’t exist yet.

 - Excellent cross functional leadership across Engineering, Design, Security, Legal, Compliance, Operations and external partners.

 - A bias toward simplifying complicated systems rather than layering more complexity on top of them.

NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience with open banking, Canada’s consumer-driven banking framework, or building to a data sharing standard

 - A background in financial data aggregation, whether at an aggregator, a bank, or a fintech consuming one

 - Experience shipping a public API or developer platform as a commercial product, including partner onboarding and support

WHAT GREAT LOOKS LIKE

You won’t just operate Bank Linking and ship API endpoints.

You’ll create a coherent connectivity strategy for Wealthsimple: making it easier for clients to bring their financial life to Wealthsimple, easier to move their financial data where they want it to go, easier for any team at Wealthsimple to build on that data, and increasingly less dependent on the slow pace of connectivity innovation from incumbent financial institutions.

You’ll also have made the case for what this platform should become — the metrics, the roadmap and the investment argument that get it there.

WHY WEALTHSIMPLE?

🌸 Top-tier health benefits and life insurance

ABOUT THIS ROLE

Hi, I’m Denise https://www.linkedin.com/in/deniseeures/, and I’m the Head of High-Touch (Mid-Market) Customer Success at Ashby. Our team is passionate about shaping and scaling an exceptional customer experience for our high-touch customer segment, which primarily supports mid-market and growth-stage organizations. I’m excited to be hiring our next CSM as we continue expanding globally.

As a member of our Customer Success team, you will help us continue to grow our High-Touch Customer Success function. In this role, you’ll partner closely with customers to drive adoption, deliver strategic guidance, conduct product trainings and partnership reviews, and identify opportunities for expanded use cases and long-term value realization. You’ll also collaborate with a talented group of CSMs across the High-Touch team to continuously evolve how we support companies ranging from high-growth startups to public enterprises.

Ashby is designed to be powerful and flexible, allowing customers to tailor the platform to their unique hiring processes and workflows. Because of this, there is a lot to learn. You will become both a product and domain expert, enabling customers to make the most of Ashby and drive hiring excellence across their organizations.

Role Requirements:

 - You have a strong track record of Customer Success experience in B2B SaaS (at least two years), supporting customers through the adoption and long-term optimization of complex technologies. You enjoy building trusted partnerships with customers and helping them realize measurable value throughout the customer lifecycle.

 - You have experience managing a portfolio of approximately 60 mid-market customers with over $1.5M in total ARR. You’re comfortable balancing proactive engagement across a broad book of business while building strong relationships with a diverse set of stakeholders to drive adoption, retention, and growth.

 - You have experience partnering cross-functionally with teams such as Sales, Marketing, Product, Support, and Operations to advocate for customer needs and deliver a seamless customer experience.

 - You enjoy becoming a product expert and have demonstrated this in previous Customer Success roles. You create “aha” moments by tailoring trainings, workflow guidance, and strategic recommendations to each customer’s unique goals and challenges.

 - You’ve worked with technically complex products and bring strong curiosity and problem-solving skills to understanding how systems, workflows, and integrations operate in practice

You Should Apply If:

 - 📣 You demonstrate mastery of clear communication. You ask questions with precision and can explain complex concepts in simple terms. 

 - 🎧 You are a great listener. You see your role as providing the voice of the customer to internal stakeholders so we can ensure that our product roadmap continues delivering value.

 - 📊You enjoy working with a larger book of varied customers, and can effectively prioritise your time to make the biggest impact.

 - 🧩 You’re energized by learning and supporting a complex product. You enjoy diving deep into technical details, navigating advanced configurations, and data workflows, and you enjoy helping customers make sense of them.

 - 🧑‍🏫 You love to teach. Whether it’s a complex report to a very tenured data analyst, or a workflow to a brand new recruiter, who is new to SaaS tools, you see every teaching moment as an opportunity.

 - 🔍 Your peers describe you as detail oriented. You obsess over sending crisp follow-up emails, on time. You take pride in internal operations, like real-time CRM updates.

 - ⚡️ You move fast. You leverage tools/technology to maximize your time. You are at home managing a wide range of customers, and prioritizing effectively.

 - 🗺️ You're energized by an ever-improving work environment. Our team is growing, and continually iterating on processes - we live by our Operating Principle of "Implement Continuous Improvement"

 - 📊 You are always looking for ways to improve your work through data.

Why you shouldn’t apply:

 - You thrive with a smaller, more focused book of customers,. Our Mid-Market CSMs typically manage a book of 60+ customers, balancing personalized relationships with efficient, scalable support.

 - You're interested in managing customer accounts with well-defined touchpoints (rather than excited by the fluidity required of early stage CS work)

 - You shine as an exclusively commercial CSM, motivated by variable compensation. While our team's north star metric is revenue retention, we focus on adoption and engagement as our leading indicators. For renewal negotiation and upsell, we have a lovely team of Contract Managers. As such, this role does not currently include variable pay.

 - You’re afraid of rolling up your sleeves. If the idea of getting in the weeds with a customer about the nuance between a time in process report and a time to hire report feels too granular, or project managing a workflow change for offer approvals feels “beneath you”, this job isn’t going to be for you.

ABOUT ASHBY

We’re building the next generation of enterprise software, and we’re starting with a suite of products that help talent leaders, recruiters, and hiring managers run their hiring process significantly better. Learn more on our website:  https://www.ashbyhq.com/%EF%BF%BC%EF%BF%BCWehttps://www.ashbyhq.com/

We are well funded and backed by great investors, including Y Combinator, Elad Gil and Lachy Groom. We have thousands of amazing customers including Snowflake, OpenAI, Shopify, Ramp, Notion, and Zapier (and many others who we cannot name!). Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in ARR, growing >100% year over year, very low churn, and many years of runway. We’ll share more details once we meet. In short, it's the perfect time to join! 🚀

INTERVIEW PROCESS

Our interview process is thorough - we aim to ensure each person that joins the team is the right fit for Ashby and will provide ample information for you to assess if Ashby is the right fit for you. The process for this role is as follows:

 - Intro Call with Ashby Recruiting - 30 Minutes

 - Hiring Manager Interview - 45 Minutes

 - Mock Customer Call - 45 Minutes

 - Final Round - 1 hour
   
   - Rather than a traditional panel interview with a large group, we structure our panel into two focused conversations. This gives you the opportunity to meet with multiple team members in a more conversational setting centered on specific topics, instead of a formal Q&A. You'll discuss how you approach problem solving, dive into a product complexity exercise, then wrap up with a quick closing call with the hiring manager.

BENEFITS

Wealthsimple is Canada’s leading financial innovator. The company offers a full suite of simple, sophisticated financial products across managed investing, do-it-yourself trading, cryptocurrency, tax filing, spending and saving. Wealthsimple currently serves more than 4 million Canadians and holds over $169 billion in assets under administration. The company was founded in 2014 by a team of financial experts and technology entrepreneurs, and is headquartered in Toronto, Canada.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a Growth Manager to own performance and lifecycle marketing for our active trader and crypto business. This role runs the programs that grow our self-directed trading and crypto segment - acquiring high-intent traders and crypto investors through the channels they live in, converting them into funded active traders, and deepening engagement through lifecycle across the trades, products, and benefits that drive volume and revenue.

You'll own paid media and lifecycle end-to-end, from media buys on trader and crypto-native channels through in-app journeys that turn a new account into an active, funded trader. You'll partner closely with Product, Product Marketing, Lifecycle, Sales/BDR, and Analytics; operate with a high degree of day-to-day autonomy; and be accountable for funded active-trader and crypto engagement outcomes.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own active trader and crypto demand generation across the channels traders and crypto investors live in — paid social (X/Twitter, Cashtags), trading platforms (TradingView), finance and crypto media (Yahoo Finance), trading and crypto newsletters, SEM, and influencers/community — measured through to funded accounts and sustained trading activity, not clicks.

 - Own the media buys end to end — plan and manage budgets, negotiate placements and rates with vendors, run creative and landing-page testing, and diagnose what's working (reactivation vs. acquisition, channel vs. landing page) rather than just reporting spend.

 - Own the trader and crypto lifecycle alongside Lifecycle and Product — activation, first-trade, funding, and "nearly active" re-engagement journeys across Braze content cards, AT status screens, and rewards. Bring performance and LCM best practices to how these journeys are built, even where you're not hands-on-keyboard for every send.

 - Drive go-to-market for active trader and crypto products and benefits — options, futures, margin, USD, and crypto (spread pricing, coin selection, staking) — coordinating paid, lifecycle, web, and product surfaces into a single launch, and owning the brief end to end.

 - Build and maintain clear reporting across the trader and crypto funnel — first touch through sign-up, funding, first trade, and retained trading value. Partner with Analytics on incrementality and true lift, and make clear recommendations on where to double down, test, or pull back.

 - Run a consistent testing cadence across creative, audiences, offers, and landing pages, and turn what you learn into repeatable programs.

 - Actively embed AI tools into performance and lifecycle workflows — creative and copy iteration, audience research, landing page iteration, and campaign experimentation.

 - Contribute to the quarterly plan alongside other Growth leads, then own delivery against it.
   

WHAT YOU BRING

 - 4–6 years in performance marketing, growth, or lifecycle marketing with a track record of generating high-quality consumer demand and optimizing it through to downstream value.

 - Deep hands-on experience in paid media — you've owned budgets and managed campaigns across platforms like Google, Meta, X, YouTube, or programmatic, negotiated with vendors, and optimized for downstream value rather than cost per click.

 - Lifecycle marketing depth — you've built or owned activation, onboarding, nurture, or re-engagement journeys and understand how lifecycle compounds the demand you generate. Hands-on with a lifecycle platform (Braze, Iterable, HubSpot, or similar) is strongly preferred; at minimum you bring the best practices and can direct the work.

 - Experience marketing to engaged, high-intent audiences who know the product and compare it closely to alternatives — you understand how messaging, channel mix, and creative shift for that kind of buyer.

 - Strong cross-functional partnering — you've worked closely with Product and Analytics (segment definitions, funnel diagnosis, incrementality) and Product Marketing (messaging, GTM briefs), and made those relationships an advantage.

 - A demonstrated habit of using AI to accelerate your work — creative at scale, research and enrichment workflows, faster insight from data. You treat AI as a core part of how you work.

 - Analytical mindset — you use data to diagnose funnel problems, prioritize opportunities, and recommend change, not just report on results.
   

NICE TO HAVES:

 - Personal or professional familiarity with self-directed investing, active trading, or crypto — options, margin, futures, high-frequency trading, or digital assets — and the platforms and communities traders live in (X/FinTwit, TradingView, trading and crypto newsletters, YouTube).

 - Experience running go-to-market for a product or benefit launch across paid, lifecycle, and product surfaces.

 - Experience in consumer fintech, investing, brokerage, trading, or crypto platforms.

WHO ARE WE?

WHY THIS ROLE?

We’re building the foundational infrastructure that will define how the world thinks about and deploys AI, and we want the sharpest, most driven, and most curious people to help us do it. As the head of the Data Foundation pillar of our Analytics and Data Insights team, you’ll lead the team that makes Cohere’s data trustworthy, governed, and available: the warehouse every analytics surface runs on, the pipelines that keep it fresh, the access model that keeps it secure, and the agentic analytics layer that lets anyone at Cohere (and their agents) ask questions of governed data directly.

Your team owns the full data lifecycle. You’ll run ingestion into BigQuery from internal and external data sources, orchestrate it in Airflow and Cloud Run, model the data warehouse in dbt, and serve the results through Looker, export APIs, and customer-facing analytics surfaces. Everything is provisioned as code in Terraform, and governance is part of the design: VPC service controls, IAM patterns, and documented access paths that let people and agents move fast without putting data at risk.

This role is both highly visible and highly impactful, and you’ll inherit a solid structure on which to build the rest of the stack: a Terraform-provisioned warehouse framework, dbt modeling conventions, an alerting and incident-response practice, and documentation patterns to keep everything discoverable. The roadmap is set with big bets in flight: scaling that framework across the company, standing up an internal analytics agent with a real eval harness, and consolidating institutional knowledge into a self-correcting and self-maintaining system that keeps context centralized, current, and documented, rather than dispersed and in people’s heads.

Responsibilities

As the head of the Data Foundation pillar, you will:

 - Build and lead the team. Hire and grow a team of data and infrastructure engineers; set the technical bar; develop strong talent and raise team performance, building leadership capability beneath you.

 - Set the roadmap from company strategy. Own and sequence the Data Foundation roadmap: the warehouse buildout, the agentic analytics program, data governance, and the platform work that unblocks our other pillars. You’ll make the trade-offs and carry the cross-functional impact that comes with them.

 - Own the data platform end to end. Ingestion (managed connectors and an open-source connector framework), orchestration on Airflow and Cloud Run, warehouse modeling in BigQuery with dbt (raw, core, mart layers), and serving through Looker, export APIs, and semantic layers. All of it provisioned as code in Terraform.

 - Own data governance. Define how humans, service accounts, and agents get access to governed data: VPC service controls, IAM patterns, documented onboarding paths, audit logs, and sensitive requests (including legal holds) handled to deadline.

 - Operate for reliability. Run the alerting and anomaly-detection framework, own data freshness SLAs, lead incident response and postmortems, and turn every incident into a durable standard so the same class of failure doesn’t recur.

 - Lead the agentic analytics program. Wire the semantic layer into an internal analytics agent, build the eval harness that measures its accuracy, and make the eval-driven call on where AI earns its way into production. Apply the same discipline to automating data engineering work itself.

 - Set the standard for analytics across the company. The medallion framework, naming conventions, and testing patterns your team maintains become the way other teams ship analytics data. You’ll onboard new domains onto it and keep the docs accurate to how the systems actually work.

 - Partner across the org. Work with the North product and engineering teams on the analytics surfaces that ship in the product (including a customer-facing analytics export), with Business Insights on marts for the business, with Security on data governance, and with Legal on compliance-critical data requests.

QUALIFICATIONS

You may be a good fit, if you have:

 - 10+ years of experience across data engineering, data infrastructure, or analytics platform work, with a strong management track record leading data platform or infrastructure teams

 - Serious hands-on history in data engineering or infrastructure before management. You can still read a Terraform plan, a dbt DAG, or an Airflow scheduler log and ask the question that matters

 - Production experience with cloud data warehouses (BigQuery, Snowflake, or similar), workflow orchestration (Airflow or similar), and infrastructure as code (Terraform or similar)

 - Depth in data modeling: you think in fact and dimension tables, raw/core/mart separation, and semantic layers, and you have opinions on where tests and contracts belong

 - A record of setting a team’s roadmap from company or function strategy and delivering outcomes that span teams, with the cross-functional partnerships to match

 - Operational excellence you can point to: alerting you trust, SLAs you meet, incidents you run to ground and write up so they teach

 - Exposure to data security and governance: IAM, access management, VPC service controls or equivalent, audit and compliance workflows

 - Genuine excitement about AI: you follow the research, have opinions, and are energized by building the data foundation an AI company (and its AI agents) runs on

 - Comfort operating in ambiguity, leading a multi-workstream roadmap, and working directly with executives on priorities

If some of the above doesn’t line up perfectly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply!

Mindrift connects specialists with project-based AI opportunities for leading tech companies, focused on testing, evaluating, and improving AI systems. Participation is project-based and is not an employment relationship.
 What this opportunity involves 
 We're looking for contributors to share their own medical lab report. You add the original files, and details that identify you, such as names, ID numbers, dates of birth, and contact details, are covered automatically and checked again during review before the report is used. You also check the redacted preview before you submit. The lab's name and address, the test names, and the results stay in the report. Once your report is accepted, it is no longer linked to you. The files help improve AI systems that read and understand medical documents. In this project, contributors may:
 Add the PDF file of their own lab report, for example blood test results;
 Take an iPhone photo of each printed page of the report and a screenshot of each page on an iPhone, iPad, or Mac;
 Check the redacted preview of each page and submit it only if all details that identify them are covered;
 Add one report per task;
 Submit clear files where every page of the report is fully visible.
 If you have your own lab test results and are comfortable sharing them once your personal details are covered, apply to take part in this project.
 What we look for 
 This opportunity is a good fit for people who have their own lab test results and are open to a short-term, project-based collaboration. To take part, contributors will need:
 To be 18 to 65 years old and live in one of these countries: the UK, Canada, Ireland, Germany, Switzerland, Poland, Portugal, Brazil, Spain, Türkiye, Norway, Indonesia, the UAE, or Israel (no VPN while using Mindrift);
 Their own medical lab report as a PDF file (1 to 10 pages): lab test results only, such as a blood count, blood chemistry, or a urine test;
 A report from a lab in the country where they live, preferably in the local language (reports in English, or in both languages, are also accepted);
 A printed copy of the report, an iPhone (any model) for the photos, and an iPhone, iPad, or Mac for the screenshots.
 This opportunity is not suitable for someone else’s lab report (for example, a family member’s), a translated or edited copy of a report, or other medical documents such as discharge summaries or surgery notes. 
 How it works  
 Apply → Get an email from Mindrift Team (check spam too) → Register on Mindrift → Verify your identity → Sign the project consent form → Add your report's PDF, photos, and screenshots and check the redacted preview → Get paid for each accepted report 
 Privacy
 Taking part is voluntary, and choosing not to take part doesn’t affect your Mindrift account. Before your first task, you read and sign a project consent form. Details that identify you, such as names, ID numbers, dates of birth, addresses, phone numbers, and email addresses, as well as doctors' names and signatures, are covered automatically and checked again during review before the report is used. Your original files are deleted. Once your report is accepted, it is no longer linked to you. We never ask you to send your report by email, chat or anywhere outside the Mindrift platform.
 Project time expectations 
 Each lab report is a separate task, and you can add reports whenever it suits you while the project is active. This is a time-limited project, and the number of reports we can accept is not guaranteed. Reports need to meet the listed criteria to be accepted. If a report needs a fix, it comes back to you with the reason. 
 Earnings  
 Paid per accepted report:  $10 for every lab report  (PDF, photos, and screenshots of each page) that passes our quality checks. Earnings are added to your Mindrift balance once the report is accepted. 
 You can withdraw them to your bank account or PayPal via Tipalti, or via Payoneer (minimum $20). Payouts are processed twice a month. Mindrift doesn't deduct any fees, but your payment provider may charge a small transfer fee.

About ServiceCentral
 ServiceCentral builds the software that runs product service after the sale: warranty claims, repair authorization, and service execution, for everyone from the local repair shop to the Fortune 50 OEM. We have been doing it for 25+ years. We are Dell's Partner of the Year, two years running, and our products run service operations across 1,200+ locations in 100+ countries. We are backed by Valsoft Corporation, a permanent-capital owner of 150+ vertical software companies, so we build for the next decade, not the next funding round.
 The Role
 ServiceCentral is hiring Partnership & Growth Associates to win new customers and grow the ones we bring in. This is a real sales role from day one: you will build your own pipeline, run your own discovery conversations, deliver your own demos, and carry a quota. New business is the priority here, and prospecting is not something you fit around the edges of your week, it is the heart of the job.
 You will also own accounts outright, which means you get to see the full arc of a customer relationship rather than one slice of it: winning them, getting them live, growing them, and keeping them. You will build real product depth, get hands-on coaching from people who have done this work themselves, and have experienced support in the room when a deal gets complex. What we are looking for in return is drive, curiosity, and a genuine appetite for hitting a number.
 What You Will Own
 Pipeline generation and conversion
 Generate qualified pipeline through outbound calling, email sequences, and social outreach across assigned campaigns, verticals, and territories
 Sustain consistent, high-volume prospecting activity as the anchor of your week
 Manage and qualify inbound leads with fast, accurate follow-up and correct routing
 Research accounts and stakeholders so outreach is personalised rather than generic
 Run discovery conversations using our qualification framework, and deliver online product demonstrations
 Close new business against a quarterly quota
 Hand off opportunities above your authority to Specialists, Managers, or Directors with full context, and earn sourced-pipeline credit
 Route opportunities on the other platform to your counterpart owner, and earn referral credit
 Account ownership
 Own the full commercial relationship for your assigned portfolio of accounts
 Maintain a defined contact cadence so no owned account drifts without engagement
 Execute standard renewals cleanly and on time
 Identify upsell and cross-sell opportunities, closing the simple ones and pulling in a Manager or Director on the rest
 Monitor account health signals and flag at-risk relationships early, before they become recoveries
 Execute defined save plays on accounts showing risk
 Onboarding and time to value
 Own commercial handoff and welcome communications that set clear expectations
 Coordinate onboarding with Solutions and Support so customers reach value quickly
 Track time-to-first-value on your accounts and intervene when it slips
 Act on or route expansion signals that surface during onboarding
 Revenue integrity
 Audit subscription billing on your accounts to prevent revenue leakage
 Monitor involuntary churn signals (failed and declined charges) and drive resolution within 24 hours
 Reconcile the billing platform against internal records so MRR reporting is accurate
 Verify plan changes (upgrades, downgrades, cancellations) are executed correctly before a customer notices an error
 Surface systemic billing patterns to your Manager rather than fixing the same problem repeatedly
 Enablement and team support
 Provide day-to-day support on larger accounts held by senior colleagues: routine maintenance, data updates, configuration changes, and low-complexity requests
 Absorb repeatable work so senior capacity stays on new business and strategic pursuits
 Create and maintain customer-facing Knowledge Base and self-service content that drives adoption and reduces inbound volume
 Verify release notes for accuracy and customer clarity before publication
 Support go-to-market materials and campaign content for upsell and cross-sell motions
 Support trade shows and events: booth materials, collateral, demo environment readiness, on-site coordination, and lead capture with follow-up
 Systems discipline
 Keep CRM records complete and current, with a scheduled next action on every open opportunity
 Log activity accurately, because your forecast and your credit both depend on it
 What We Are Looking For
 Commercial drive.  You want to carry a number and you want to beat it.
 Resilience.  High-volume outreach means high-volume rejection. You need to make the next call sound like the first one.
 Coachability.  This tier exists partly to develop you. The people who progress fastest ask for feedback and visibly act on it.
 Process discipline.  You will run recurring operational workflows (billing audits, cadence management, CRM hygiene) that protect revenue. Reliability here is the foundation of customer trust.
 Commercial instinct.  You notice when a routine support question is actually an expansion signal, and you do something about it.
 Clear written communication.  Your emails, customer-facing content, and CRM notes are all read by someone who will judge us on them.
 Customer empathy.  You will handle billing disputes and pricing conversations. Doing that well protects both the relationship and the revenue.
 Curiosity about the platform.  The Associates who become Specialists learned their platform properly, not just the pitch.
 Autonomy and Escalation
 You operate inside a structured playbook with a clear escalation path. Escalation is a strength at this tier, not a weakness.
 Decide yourself:  standard pricing and terms, routine renewals, day-to-day account management within cadence.
 Escalate: 
 Any discount request, however small
 Any at-risk account signal, immediately
 Billing discrepancies above defined thresholds
 Growth opportunities in your accounts that need a Manager or Director, routed with full context
 Requests for non-standard contract terms, service commitments, or SLAs
 Quota and Compensation
 You will carry a quarterly quota weighted heavily toward new business, with expansion and renewal making up the balance. Quota is set from your assigned accounts and territory rather than a generic benchmark, and it ramps across your first two quarters so you are not held to full target while you are still learning.
 Compensation is a competitive base plus variable, with the variable tied to new business won, pipeline quality, and team performance. We will walk you through targets, weightings, and exactly how performance is measured during the interview process.
 Where This Leads
 Associate is the first rung of a four-tier track. Typical progression to  Partnership & Growth Specialist  takes 12 to 24 months.
 To be promoted you will need to show: 
 Two consecutive quarters at or above quota
 Clean, independent ownership of your named accounts
 Ability to run discovery unsupervised
 Evidence you have informally coached at least one peer
 Compensation and logistics
 On-target earnings: $130k CAD  (base ~$50-70k plus variable). Variable is tied to closed-won new business. When our MD or CCO leads the close on an enterprise deal, you share in the win for the pipeline you built and advanced
 Full benefits
 Remote within Canada, with working hours that overlap Eastern Time, where most of our team sits. 
 Some travel expected, predominantly within North America

À PROPOS DE POWER FACTORS
 L’OPPORTUNITÉ
 Power Factors est à la recherche d’un·e vice-président·e, Contrôleur·euse expérimenté·e pour diriger l’organisation mondiale de comptabilité et de contrôle financier de l’entreprise dans un environnement SaaS et technologique international et complexe.
 Relevant du ou de la chef·fe de la direction financière, le ou la vice-président·e, Contrôleur·euse est un membre clé de l’équipe de direction des Finances et un·e partenaire de confiance du ou de la chef·fe de la direction financière en matière de comptabilité, de gouvernance financière, de risque, d’évolutivité opérationnelle et de transformation des Finances. Le rôle est responsable de l’intégrité, de l’exactitude et de l’évolutivité des activités comptables mondiales de l’entreprise, y compris la clôture financière et la production de rapports, la comptabilisation des revenus, les comptes clients, les comptes fournisseurs, les contrôles financiers, la comptabilité statutaire et les activités financières connexes.
 Il s’agit d’un rôle de leadership à la fois stratégique et concret. La personne retenue allie une solide expertise technique en comptabilité à un leadership opérationnel et renforcera les processus, les contrôles, les systèmes, la discipline de trésorerie et les capacités organisationnelles à mesure que Power Factors poursuit sa croissance à l’échelle mondiale. Le rôle contribuera à bâtir un modèle de contrôle financier évolutif qui soutient plusieurs entités, devises, juridictions et modèles commerciaux en évolution.
 CE QUE VOUS FEREZ
 Comptabilité mondiale et contrôle financier 
 Diriger la fonction mondiale de comptabilité et de contrôle financier de l’entreprise, en assurant une information financière exacte, à jour et uniforme dans l’ensemble des entités et des juridictions.
 Assumer la responsabilité des processus de clôture financière mensuelle, trimestrielle et annuelle et améliorer continuellement la rapidité, la qualité et la prévisibilité de la clôture.
 S’assurer que des politiques, procédures, contrôles, rapprochements et documents comptables appropriés sont en place dans toute l’organisation.
 Superviser les activités de comptabilité générale, y compris le grand livre, la comptabilité intersociétés, les charges à payer, les charges payées d’avance, les immobilisations et les rapprochements de bilan.
 Assurer l’application uniforme des politiques comptables dans les entités mondiales et repérer de façon proactive les risques comptables émergents.
 Information financière, gouvernance et conformité 
 Superviser la préparation et l’intégrité des états financiers consolidés et des rapports de gestion.
 Maintenir de solides contrôles financiers et une gouvernance appropriée des processus financiers, avec des responsabilités et des mécanismes d’escalade clairs.
 Diriger le processus d’audit externe et agir à titre de principal point de contact pour les auditeurs externes et les conseillers en comptabilité.
 Assurer la conformité aux normes comptables applicables et aux exigences de production de rapports statutaires dans les entités internationales.
 Collaborer avec les équipes Fiscalité, Affaires juridiques, Paie et Personnes et culture pour soutenir les exigences réglementaires, statutaires et de conformité des entités.
 Agir à titre de partenaire clé du ou de la chef·fe de la direction financière en matière de comptabilité, de gouvernance financière, de risque, d’évolutivité opérationnelle et de priorités de transformation des Finances.
 Comptabilisation des revenus 
 Diriger le cadre comptable d’un environnement de revenus mondial complexe couvrant les abonnements SaaS, les services professionnels, les projets, les ententes de mise en œuvre et d’autres contrats clients.
 Assumer la responsabilité des politiques de comptabilisation des revenus, des évaluations de contrats, des processus, des rapprochements et des contrôles, en assurant une application exacte et uniforme dans l’ensemble de l’entreprise. La connaissance de la comptabilisation des revenus au fil du temps selon l’ASC 606 est un atout.
 Collaborer avec les Opérations des revenus, la Planification et analyse financières (FP&A), les Ventes, les Services professionnels, les Affaires juridiques et d’autres équipes de l’entreprise pour assurer une information sur les revenus exacte et à jour.

 Renforcer les processus et les contrôles liés aux revenus à mesure que l’entreprise et ses modèles commerciaux évoluent.
 Opérations comptables et fonds de roulement

 Établir une solide discipline opérationnelle en matière de facturation, de recouvrement, d’affectation des encaissements, de paiements aux fournisseurs, de charges à payer et de rapprochements.

 S’assurer que les opérations comptables soutiennent efficacement plusieurs entités juridiques, devises et juridictions.
 Trésorerie et gestion des liquidités 
 Gérer les relations de l’entreprise avec ses banques et ses institutions financières.
 Superviser le parc de comptes bancaires, en rationaliser le nombre et assurer un environnement de contrôle approprié.
 Diriger la gestion mondiale des liquidités et de la trésorerie : financement des sociétés affiliées, rapatriement de la trésorerie et placements, conformément à la politique et à la tolérance au risque.
 Gérer les instruments de financement du commerce, y compris la négociation et l’émission de cautionnements et de garanties.
 Superviser les systèmes de trésorerie et leur environnement d’intégration, en assurant la connectivité bancaire et l’intégration aux systèmes financiers.
 Superviser la gestion des prêts et de la dette, y compris les reports de soldes et la tenue des livres.
 Systèmes, processus, transformation et intégration 
 Bâtir un modèle opérationnel de contrôle financier mondial évolutif en normalisant les processus, en éliminant les activités manuelles inutiles, en renforçant l’utilisation des systèmes et en recourant à l’automatisation et à l’IA lorsque approprié.
 Renforcer l’utilisation des systèmes et des données financières afin d’améliorer l’exactitude, l’évolutivité, la transparence et le soutien à la prise de décisions.

 S’assurer que les processus et les systèmes sont évolutifs dans plusieurs entités, devises et juridictions, ainsi que pour la croissance future de l’entreprise.
 Leadership et organisation 
 Diriger, former et encadrer une organisation comptable répartie sur plusieurs régions géographiques.
 Bâtir une solide capacité de leadership, une profondeur technique et une relève au sein de l’équipe des Finances.
 Établir des responsabilités, des priorités, des droits de décision et des rythmes opérationnels clairs dans toute l’organisation de contrôle financier.
 Développer une organisation capable de concilier une gouvernance financière rigoureuse et un soutien réactif et pragmatique à l’entreprise.
 Collaborer étroitement avec le ou la chef·fe de la direction financière, la FP&A, les Opérations des revenus, la Fiscalité, les Affaires juridiques, Personnes et culture et les leaders opérationnels.

 12 ans et plus d’expérience progressive en comptabilité, en contrôle financier, en information financière ou dans des rôles de leadership connexes en finance.
 Expérience significative de leadership à titre de contrôleur·euse, de contrôleur·euse corporatif·ive, de vice-président·e Comptabilité ou dans un rôle senior de contrôle financier au sein d’une organisation mondiale complexe.
 Titre comptable professionnel tel que CPA, CA, CMA, ACCA ou l’équivalent.
 Solide expertise technique en comptabilité et en information financière, avec un bon jugement dans des situations complexes ou en évolution.
 Expérience de la direction d’opérations comptables dans plusieurs entités juridiques, devises et juridictions.
 Expérience démontrée de la gestion de la clôture mensuelle et de fin d’exercice, des audits externes, des contrôles financiers et de l’information statutaire.
 Bonne compréhension de la comptabilisation des revenus et expérience dans un environnement d’abonnement, SaaS, technologique ou de revenus tout aussi complexe, y compris des ententes comportant des volets de services ou de mise en œuvre.
 Expérience de la direction et du développement d’équipes financières réparties sur plusieurs régions géographiques.
 Succès démontré dans l’amélioration, la normalisation et l’automatisation des processus comptables et dans l’établissement d’indicateurs opérationnels significatifs.
 Solide expérience des ERP et des systèmes financiers; l’expérience avec NetSuite est fortement souhaitable.
 L’expérience du soutien aux acquisitions, de la comptabilisation des acquisitions ou de l’intégration après acquisition est un atout.
 Capacité à évoluer efficacement dans une organisation dynamique et en évolution, et à passer aisément du leadership stratégique aux enjeux opérationnels détaillés.

Description 
 Chez Tecsys, les logiciels que nous livrons permettent aux hôpitaux, aux pharmacies et aux distributeurs d’obtenir ce dont ils ont besoin, au moment où ils en ont besoin. Chaque rôle contribue à ce résultat.
 Pourquoi ce rôle est important 
 Chaque hôpital, entrepôt et centre de distribution qui utilise Tecsys est relié à des dizaines d’autres systèmes : PGI (ERP), DME (EMR), plateformes de commerce électronique et d’automatisation. Lorsque ces connexions échouent, des soins peuvent être retardés et des marchandises bloquées. Nous bâtissons de toutes nouvelles plateformes d’intégration, avec l’IA au cœur de notre façon de travailler, et nous recherchons la personne qui veillera à ce qu’elles fonctionnent à tout coup. Si vous préférez façonner l’avenir plutôt qu’hériter du passé, ce poste est pour vous.
 Ce dont vous ferez partie 
 Tecsys a la confiance d’organisations aux activités essentielles dans les secteurs de la santé et de la distribution pour propulser des chaînes d’approvisionnement résilientes, efficaces et sécurisées. Nous sommes un fournisseur mondial de logiciels infonuagiques propulsés par l’IA, inscrit à la Bourse de Toronto (TSX : TCS).
 Trois valeurs guident notre façon de travailler. Nous gagnons la confiance chaque jour en valorisant le client et en agissant avec intégrité. Nous nous soutenons mutuellement en reconnaissant les forces de chacun et en travaillant comme une seule équipe. Et nous explorons avec audace en restant curieux et en nous adaptant pour réussir.
 Vous joindrez une culture animée par la curiosité, l’apprentissage continu et des personnes qui repoussent les limites du possible.
 Ce que vous ferez 
 À titre d’analyste AQ au sein de notre équipe Intégrations, vous testerez les API, les couches de transformation et les flux de données qui acheminent les commandes, les stocks et les expéditions entre Tecsys et les systèmes tiers, et vous contribuerez à définir comment la qualité est intégrée à nos plateformes de nouvelle génération. Vous devrez :
 Tester les API REST et SOAP et les couches de transformation dorsales, en validant les charges utiles, les mappages et l’intégrité des données de bout en bout
 Définir la stratégie de test et les critères d’acceptation avec les équipes de développement et de produit, de la conception à la production
 Utiliser l’IA au cœur de votre travail pour générer des cas et des données de test, bâtir des suites automatisées et analyser les échecs
 Rédiger et maintenir des tests automatisés d’API et d’intégration exécutés dans nos pipelines CI/CD
 Planifier et réaliser des tests de performance et de charge sur les flux d’intégration
 Tester des intégrations sur AWS en utilisant les journaux, les files d’attente et les bases de données pour retracer les données entre les systèmes
 Suivre les anomalies et les résultats dans Jira, et contribuer à évaluer de nouveaux outils et de meilleures façons de tester
 Ce que vous apportez

Why this role?

The Data Infrastructure team at Cohere is responsible for the storage and data movement layer underlying every model training run. We're building the unified storage layer that feeds our training workloads. It needs to serve petabytes of training data and model checkpoints fast enough to keep thousands of GPUs busy across several training clusters. In this role, you’d have an opportunity to build this system from the ground up. You’d be a key contributor, working on a problem few teams have had to solve at this scale.

In this role, you will:

 - Design, build, and operate the distributed storage system that feeds model training and evaluation.

 - Run this system multiple on Kubernetes clusters at petabyte scale.

 - Work with researchers and training-infra teams on how jobs actually read and write data, and turn that into throughput, latency, and durability requirements

 - Work through the networking, I/O, and consistency problems of moving large datasets and checkpoints across regions and backends, with GPU idle time and time-to-insight as the measures of success
   

You may be a good fit if you have:

 - Strong storage fundamentals, including replication, consistency, caching, and data lifecycle management.

 - Strong coding ability. We work in Python and Go; experience in either is enough, but you should be willing to pick up the other

 - Experience running stateful systems on Kubernetes, including Persistent Volumes, CSI drivers, and StatefulSets.

 - Hands-on experience with cloud object storage such as S3 as well as POSIX-style filesystems.
   

It’s a bonus if you have:

 - Experience with parallel or HPC filesystems such as Weka, VAST, or Lustre.

 - Familiarity with the data-loading and checkpointing patterns used in large-scale model training.

 - An interest in how large models are trained and evaluated, including the trajectory and eval data those runs generate, and a desire to understand the workloads the platform is serving.
